title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Client Under a Disability
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal is representing an elderly client in an eviction matter. Over the course of the representation, the paralegal notices that the client's memory is deteriorating significantly and they appear to lack the capacity to give clear legal instructions. What is the paralegal's obligation?
options: Make decisions on the client's behalf based on what the paralegal thinks is best for them.
Maintain a normal paralegal-client relationship as much as reasonably possible and consider taking steps to have a litigation guardian appointed.
Contact the opposing party to inform them that the client lacks mental capacity.
questions.explain: Rule 3.02 (Clients under a Disability) states that when a client's ability to make decisions is impaired, the paralegal shall, as far as reasonably possible, maintain a normal paralegal-client relationship. The paralegal may need to take steps to protect the client's interests, such as seeing that a lawfully authorized representative (e.g., litigation guardian) is appointed.
